speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about these episodes where you wake up frightened, and do you remember any dreams or feel confused when this happens?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any specific terrifying dreams during these episodes, and have you experienced any recent stressors or changes in your daily routine? I also need to check if there is any snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you recall the bad dreams, this suggests nightmares rather than night terrors. Do you experience any snoring, gasping, or pauses in breathing while asleep? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
